$comment: PR review risk tiering. Read by ~/.claude/hooks/pr-review-policy.sh.
Any file matching 'high' => HIGH (Gitar + CodeRabbit). All files matching 'low' => LOW.
Everything else => NORMAL (Gitar only). No match anywhere => NORMAL, deliberately.
This repo has all four high-risk shapes at once: EF migrations, real Azure infra
(infra/ + infra.yml + deploy.yml), an auth surface, and a MONEY LEDGER.
AiObservatory.Data/Spend is spend-ledger persistence - the brief's worked example of
a change worth spending a CodeRabbit review on was exactly this area (PR #100, where
review caught a DateOnly vs DateTimeOffset wire-format bug against a billing API).
LOW justification for THIS repo: docs/ is developer documentation with no site build.
clients/ is generated API client code that ships - NORMAL, not low.
Markdown is '**/*.md', NOT '*.md'. A single star compiles to [^/]* and is therefore
root-anchored: README.md matched, clients/README.md did not, so a docs-only PR
touching both fell through to NORMAL.
Dependency manifests (package.json, package-lock.json, Directory.Packages.props,
**/*.csproj) were REMOVED from 'high' on 2026-07-29 and must not be added back. They are
what Dependabot edits, and dependency PRs are out of AI code review on both vendors:
CodeRabbit refuses bot authors outright and Gitar's bot review is switched off, because
reviewing every bump exhausts the allowance and starves the changes that need it. Listing
them HIGH would demand a reviewer that can never run - coverage on paper, none in fact. CI
plus Dependabot's own advisory data is what gates a bump. nuget.config, global.json, .npmrc
and Directory.Build.props stay HIGH: registry/feed and analyzer config, not bot-edited.
'.github/workflows/**' LEFT the high list on 2026-08-19 and is asserted in
review-policy-guard.yml instead, on the same reasoning that removed .gitignore on
2026-08-02: the hook tiers by path glob, so it cannot tell a permissions one-liner from
a rewrite of the deploy job, and bills a metered CodeRabbit review either way. Measured
over 100 HIGH PRs in the preceding 30 days: config-only diffs were 27 of them and
produced FOUR actionable comments between them, against 174 from code-bearing diffs,
while 45 of the 100 got no CodeRabbit verdict at all - throttled out at 73 reviews per
7 days against a 30/7d threshold. The glob was not buying review of workflow changes;
it was crowding out review of code.
Do NOT re-add it without first removing the corresponding assertions from the guard.
Deleting the guard itself needs no reviewer: "Review policy intact" is a REQUIRED
status check, so removing the workflow means the check never reports and no PR merges.
